findings.expected: Official 2023 P2 Q2 (ER PDF331): B1 'a = -2 www', B1 'b = -3 www', B1 'c = 2 www', plus 'Allow all the marks if values are seen in the correct place in the formula'. The rows are answer marks with no method mark and no answer-only exclusion (contrast Q1(b) on the same page). So the official scheme for this type awards correct values without wrong working, and the formula note extends the same award to values written inside the formula. Under OD-1's clause 'unless the official scheme for that question type awards it', the exception covers both presentations.
findings.actual: D1 scores a bare correct list 0/3 but a bare correct formula 3/3 (WO:55, :66-67). It records this split as 'D1-MOD-OD1-LIST ... the owner-binding interpretation' (WO:57), but OD-1 contains no such ruling. It also claims that the www conditions and the formula allowance are 'retained exactly in meaning'. In the app (named numeric fields a, b, c, with a formula accepted as equivalent; WO:35), a learner who fills in the requested fields gets 0 and a learner who types y=-2|x+3|+4 gets 3, for identical information.
findings.evidence: Own render ER2023 p331; WO lines cited; owner-decisions-2026-11-23.md OD-1 wording.
findings.repair: Give Vitalis one coherent rule. (A) Recommended, matching the official row: correct a, b and c with no wrong working earn B1 www each, whether given as named values or in the formula; practice feedback can still ask for the vertex/point reasoning. (B) Strict alternative: a bare list and a bare formula both earn 0, recorded as a named deviation from the official Q2 row. Remove 'owner-binding' from D1-MOD-OD1-LIST until Vitalis rules, then align WO:55-57, :66-67, exemplar :23/:53 and the MR01 authority note.

findings.expected: What the official rows credit. 2023 Q6(d), the same-type row: B1 'Under-estimate', 'Must be correct from their graph'; DB1 'Trapeziums below curve or the curve is concave'; the prose prefers trapezium-edge-below-curve wording, rejects sloping up/down, and requires reference to both curve and trapezium. No trapeziums need be drawn, because the question asks the learner to 'use your sketch' from (c). 2025 Q4(b), a different task in which the sketch sits inside the explanation part: B1 'Correct shape'; B1 F.T. 'From Their graph' for 'Over-estimate. The edges of the trapeziums are above the curve. The actual trapeziums must be drawn on the curve.' One mark covers conclusion, reason and drawn trapeziums. What D1 credits: d:B1 F.T. for the conclusion supported by the learner's own sketch; d:DB1 for a chord position relative to that curve (concavity shorthand allowed if unambiguous; 'increasing' alone rejected); no overlay required; absent sketch 0; unreadable pending.
findings.actual: Assessment: with a correct sketch, D1 equals the 2023 row. Aligning with the 2025 row would withhold credit for the verbal reason the same-type 2023 DB1 explicitly accepts, so it would misjudge learners. With a wrong-shaped sketch, the only extension beyond a strict 2023 reading is that DB1 also follows through to the learner's own curve. 2023 is silent on this, and 2025's single F.T. mark covers conclusion and reason together. With no sketch, all three schemes give 0. The hybrid therefore does not misjudge learners and is a reasonable deviation, but its disclosure misdescribes the departure. Not requiring drawn trapeziums is the 2023 standard, not a departure. Two cases are also undefined: (i) a drawn chord/trapezium overlay on the own sketch with only a brief statement (the 2025 evidence route); (ii) more than one function graph in (c). For case (ii), the 2023 prose says both graphs sketched unlabelled lost all marks for the question, and D1 removes only c:B1 and says nothing about d.

findings.repair: RECOMMENDATION: accept D1-TRAP-FT-BRIDGE with a wording change. (1) Reword it: the same-type 2023 Q6(d) row is retained in full; 'Must be correct from their graph' is read as own-graph F.T. for B1; the only extension is that DB1 is judged against the learner's own curve, supported by 2025 Q4(b), where one F.T. mark covers conclusion and reason; the 2025 drawn-trapezium condition is not adopted because it belongs to a differently worded task. (2) State that a chord/trapezium overlay drawn on the own sketch, with a statement referring to it, also earns DB1. (3) Define the multi-graph case: with no single identifiable own graph, d earns 0 unless one graph is labelled as y=ln(x-h); align c:B2/B3 with the 2023 prose or record the deviation. Vitalis decides.
